$comment: roundel's capability matrix against chalk, the package it replaces (compat-oracle's LAYERS). Rendered by <CapabilityMatrix pkg="roundel" /> from apps/docs-chassis and held by scripts/capabilities-lock.test.ts: every `ours` yes/partial names a test file and a title substring it contains, or a compat-oracle grade. chalk's cells cite chalk 6.0.0, the version compat-oracle grades, by URL: the chalk installed in this repository is 6.0.1, so a local source would not be the graded version. A row that could not be proved for every column is not here.

rows.capability: Five output modes from one rule
rows.why: `outputMode()` answers `json`, `accessible`, `ci`, `pipe` or `tty` from the runtime it is given, first match wins, so a spinner, a prompt and the help ask one question and get one answer.

chalk.note: decides a colour level and nothing else; whether to redraw is left to each package

rows.why: A user who sets `NO_COLOR` gets no colour, whatever else the environment or the command line asks for.

ours.title: NO_COLOR still beats everything, and an empty CLI_ACCESSIBLE is not set

chalk.note: its colour detection never reads NO_COLOR

rows.capability: `FORCE_COLOR=0` is never overridden by a `--color` flag
rows.why: An explicit "colour off" in the environment wins over `--color=256` or `--color=16m` on the command line, so off never turns into on.

ours.title: is never overridden into colour on

chalk.note: an environment FORCE_COLOR replaces the flag's answer before any --color level is read

rows.why: The flags chalk reads are read under the same spellings, from the argv the program hands the policy.

ours.title: colorLevel — the --color flags, when the caller hands over argv

rows.why: A flag typed for this run outranks a `FORCE_COLOR` the machine exports, so `--no-color` under `FORCE_COLOR=3` is no colour.

ours.title: the one place roundel and chalk disagree, on purpose

chalk.note: a set FORCE_COLOR replaces the flag's answer, so --no-color under FORCE_COLOR=3 is level 3

rows.capability: An agent on a terminal is not someone to prompt
rows.why: `interactive()` answers no under `CLAUDECODE`, `CURSOR_AGENT` and the other agent variables even with a terminal on stdin, so a prompt asks the one question that tells an agent from a person.

ours.title: is not interactive under %s, even on a terminal

chalk.note: decides a colour level, not whether a person can answer

rows.capability: A screen-reader mode with no colour
rows.why: With `CLI_ACCESSIBLE=1` the level is 0 even on a truecolor terminal, because escape codes are noise to a screen reader; an explicit ask still colours it.

ours.title: defaults to 0 on the most colour-capable terminal there is

rows.why: Under `--json` the level is 0 even when `FORCE_COLOR` asks for colour, so structured output never carries an escape.

ours.title: json is 0, even on a truecolor terminal, even when forced

chalk.note: has no notion of structured output; the program sets chalk.level = 0 itself

rows.capability: The decision is a pure function of a runtime
rows.why: The policy reads only the environment, arguments and terminal flag it is handed, so a test or an agent harness asks the program's question and gets the program's answer.

ours.title: reads only what the runtime carries — the same input always gives the same answer

chalk.note: reads process.env, process.argv and the file descriptors' TTY state once, at import

rows.why: A hex colour is sent as truecolor at level 3 and as the nearest of 256 or 16 colours below it.

ours.title: fall to the nearest of 256 at level 2

rows.capability: A CI vendor's colour level, once colour is asked for
rows.why: GitHub Actions, Gitea Actions and CircleCI get truecolor and the other known vendors 16 colours, while a CI pipe nobody asked to colour stays plain.

ours.title: colorLevel — the CI vendor table, once the run has asked for colour

rows.capability: Semantic tokens instead of colour names
rows.why: A program writes `error()`, `hint()` and `command()`, and the theme decides what each looks like, so the colours mean something and change together.

ours.title: level 3: the brand in truecolor, lifted for the near-black default ground

chalk.note: every colour is named at the call site

rows.capability: A theme checked for WCAG contrast
rows.why: `fly()` refuses a hex token below 4.5:1 against the declared background, at every colour level, and names the token and its ratio.

ours.title: refuses a truecolor token below 4.5:1 against the ground, naming token and ratio

chalk.note: draws any colour it is given

rows.capability: Themes through a validated plugin registry
rows.why: A plugin's tokens are validated at `register()`, a misspelt token is refused rather than dropped, and the contrast gate applies to them as to a hand-written theme.

ours.title: a misspelt token is refused, not silently dropped

rows.why: Installing it adds one package and nothing else.

ours.title: the package it installed has zero runtime dependencies (U6)

chalk.note: ansi-styles and supports-color are copied inside it

rows.why: `roundel/chalk` is graded by chalk 6.0.1's own tests, unedited, so changing the import keeps chalk's output.

chalk.note: its own suite, the control run
